correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the common k−1 core of every nontrivial TS clique by excluding Johnson top triangles, then transfers diamond-free input to diamond-free TS. Distinct maximal input cliques in diamond-free graphs cannot share an edge, yielding explicit elementary collapses of their flag simplices to a graph. Exact rook placement and core counts yield the clique polynomial; regularity, connectivity and cycle structure are proved by row/column vacancy moves and permutations. The four-cycle formula counts commuting row/column slides, and star-graph diameter is attributed. All graph-order boundary conditions checked. Standalone exhaustive finite checks include 5,405 graph/size pairs and 41 rook cases; computations corroborate the written unrestricted proof, do not substitute for it.

value.rationale: A structural flag-complex collapse for an entire hereditary input class and the closed clique enumerator and integral homotopy of all rook matching-slide graphs are natural invariants of reconfiguration spaces. Nontrivial boundary transitions in girth and a sharp four-cycle count supply mathematically meaningful distinctions. The theorem extends substantially beyond finite parameter tables and is not a mere renaming of star-graph diameter.
